news.title: Bill Ackman: Why Predictable Businesses Beat Chasing AI Hype - The Acquirer's Multiple®
news.snippet: Rather than attempting to predict short-term winners, his focus remains on ident...
news.raw_snippet: Rather than attempting to predict short-term winners, his focus remains on identifying businesses capable of compounding value over many years, regardless of market sentiment. That philosophy has become increasingly relevant as enthusiasm surrounding AI, data centers, semiconductors, and next-generation technology continues driving significant capital into a relatively small group of companies. Although Ackman is optimistic about the long-term impact of artificial intelligence, he draws an important distinction between believing in a technology and overpaying for exposure to it. As he explains, “Our strategy is to construct a portfolio of the best durable growth companies in the world, acquire them at attractive prices, and be a long-term investor.”. “Our portfolio is comprised of businesses where we with a very high degree of confidence can predict the cash flows over a very long period of time.”. As enthusiasm surrounding AI continues to dominate markets, Ackman’s comments serve as a reminder that long-term investment success depends less on chasing the newest trend and more on owning exceptional businesses purchased at sensible prices.

July 6 (Reuters) - South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix [(000660.KS), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/000660.KS) on Monday launched a U.S. share sale to raise 43 trillion won ($28.07 billion) and drew indications of interest for up to $7 billion ​from major investors, as it capitalises on the global AI boom with one of the world's largest new share sales. The company will sell 17.79 million new shares through the [ADRs](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-koreas-sk-hynix-says-raise-29-bln-us-adr-listing-2026-06-24/) on the Nasdaq; 10 ADRs will represent one common share and a Monday filing gave a reference price of 242,500 won per ADR, based on SK Hynix's July 3 closing price in Seoul. She added that SK Hynix's ADR listing was positive because it would broaden the company's investor base and potentially narrow its valuation gap with U.S rival Micron [(MU.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/MU.O). SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics [(005930.KS), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/005930.KS) will anchor the investment program, the government said.

news.title: I spoke to Anthropic's CEO about how AI may affect biotech. Here's ...
news.snippet: STAT A decade of reporting from the frontiers of health and medicine. # I spoke ...
news.raw_snippet: STAT A decade of reporting from the frontiers of health and medicine. # I spoke to Anthropic’s CEO about how AI may affect biotech. From left, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, scientist Lotte Bjerre Knudsen, and STAT’s Matthew Herper at an event to discuss Claude Science in San Francisco.Anthropic. The most convincing thing Dario Amodei, the CEO and co-founder of Anthropic, said to me during an on-stage conversation last week was that perhaps his original vision of how AI would change biotech might not start to be visible for a decade. In a 2024 essay, “Machines of Loving Grace*,*” Amodei had argued that artificial intelligence, and in particular large language models like Anthropic’s Claude, could allow researchers to make what we think of as a decade’s worth of progress every year, covering a century in a decade. Amodei and I were speaking at an Anthropic event where the company, a public-benefit corporation meant to be focused on improving the world, unveiled a product for biologists and pharmaceutical companies called Claude Science.
